terms.application-token: An application token is a credential issued by Jellyfin to an authenticated client. Browser, television and mobile clients attach it to later API and streaming requests, so Jellyfin can authorize those requests without being redirected through the separate gateway login.
terms.authentication-gateway: The authentication gateway is the small service I built on the VPS to protect selected hostnames before Caddy forwards traffic to the Pi. It applies hostname-specific account and role policies, redirecting unauthenticated browser visits while returning a 401 response to API-style requests.
terms.caddy: Caddy is the web server and reverse proxy at the public edge of this setup. It terminates HTTPS, matches each requested hostname and sends approved traffic to the corresponding Pi service through WireGuard.
terms.caddy-config-validation: Caddy can parse and validate its configuration without activating it. I run that check before a reload because one invalid site block at the shared public edge could otherwise interrupt several unrelated hostnames.
terms.caddy-forward-auth: Caddy's forward_auth directive pauses a protected request and asks another service whether it should continue. Here it calls my gateway on localhost; only an allowed result proceeds to the Pi upstream.
terms.cidr-32: In IPv4 CIDR notation, /32 identifies exactly one address rather than a larger subnet. Routing only the other peer's /32 keeps this WireGuard link focused on the two tunnel endpoints, although it does not restrict which ports can be reached on that address.
terms.cloudflare-dns: Cloudflare DNS publishes the records for hostingfrompurva.xyz. In this design those records lead to Cloudflare's proxy or the public VPS, never to the Pi or the residential internet address.
terms.cloudflare-proxy: With Cloudflare proxying enabled, a visitor connects to Cloudflare first and Cloudflare makes the next connection to the VPS. I use it for ordinary browser tools, while some long-lived media paths remain direct for simpler debugging and response handling.
terms.cloudflare-tunnel: Cloudflare Tunnel lets a private service create an outbound connection to Cloudflare instead of receiving a conventional inbound connection. I considered that model, but chose a VPS and WireGuard so I could inspect and tune the complete reverse-proxy path per hostname.
terms.dns-only: A DNS-only Cloudflare record publishes the VPS address without putting Cloudflare's HTTP proxy in the traffic path. I use that option selectively where direct handling of large or long-lived media responses is easier to understand and debug.
terms.firewall: A firewall decides which network traffic a machine will accept or reject. On this VPS it allows the web, WireGuard and SSH ports described in the article; it remains separate from WireGuard's address-routing rules.
terms.http-401: HTTP status 401 means the request lacks valid authentication credentials. The gateway returns it to API-style clients because a machine-readable failure is more appropriate than sending those clients to an HTML login page.
terms.http3: HTTP/3 carries web traffic over QUIC, which uses UDP rather than the TCP transport used by HTTP/1.1 and HTTP/2. Caddy can therefore listen on UDP 443 as well as TCP 443 for HTTPS traffic.
terms.https: HTTPS is HTTP protected by TLS. It encrypts the browser-facing connection and lets the browser verify the requested hostname; it is distinct from the WireGuard encryption used between the VPS and Pi.
terms.jellyfin: Jellyfin is the media server running on the Pi. Its clients use APIs, application tokens and long streaming responses, so Jellyfin retains playback authorization instead of having every request forced through a generic browser-login redirect.
terms.lan: The LAN is the private network inside the home. Pi services keep their normal local paths there, so a failure of the VPS or WireGuard public route should not stop local file access or television playback.
terms.localhost: Localhost refers back to the same machine, normally through 127.0.0.1. Caddy calls the authentication gateway over localhost on the VPS, so that policy endpoint does not need to be exposed as a separate public service.
terms.reverse-proxy: A reverse proxy accepts a request on behalf of an application and forwards it to the correct upstream. Caddy is the reverse proxy here: public hostnames reach the VPS, while the actual applications remain on the Pi behind WireGuard.
terms.router-port-forwarding: Router port forwarding sends traffic arriving at the home's public address to a device and port on the private network. This design avoids forwarding individual Pi application ports by making the VPS the public edge and using an outbound-friendly WireGuard route back home.
terms.secure-cookie-flags: Secure restricts the session cookie to HTTPS, HttpOnly prevents normal page scripts from reading it, and SameSite=Lax limits when browsers attach it to cross-site requests. These flags reduce common session risks, but they are not a complete replacement for application authorization or every CSRF defence.
terms.ssh: SSH provides an encrypted command-line connection to administer the VPS. It is reachable on TCP 22 in the current setup; the article calls out root and password login as hardening work rather than presenting them as safeguards.
terms.stateless-session: The gateway stores a signed session token in the browser and verifies the signature on each request instead of looking up server-side session state. That keeps the gateway simple, but an individual token cannot be centrally revoked before it expires.
terms.tailscale: Tailscale creates a private encrypted network between approved devices. It remains convenient for my own laptop and phone, but asking friends and family to join that device network was the usability problem that led to this public HTTPS path.
terms.tcp-udp-ports: TCP and UDP are transport protocols that identify receiving applications with numbered ports. This VPS accepts web traffic on TCP 80 and 443, HTTP/3 on UDP 443, WireGuard on UDP 51820 and administration through SSH on TCP 22.
terms.tls: TLS encrypts the browser-facing connection and authenticates the hostname using a certificate. In this architecture TLS protects the public web connection, while WireGuard separately protects traffic travelling from the VPS to the Pi.
terms.trust-boundary: A trust boundary is a point where data or control moves between parts of a system with different security assumptions. The VPS is public and trusted with a narrow route to the Pi, while the home LAN remains a separate boundary with no forwarded application ports.
terms.vpn: A virtual private network creates an encrypted logical network across another network such as the internet. Tailscale is convenient for Anikesh's own devices, but requiring every reader of a shared service to install a VPN client would make access unnecessarily complicated.
terms.vps: A VPS is a virtual server in a data centre with a stable public internet address. This 1-vCPU VPS is the intentionally small public edge: it runs Caddy and the authentication gateway, then reaches the Pi over WireGuard.
terms.websockets: WebSockets keep a two-way connection open so a browser and server can exchange messages without creating a new HTTP request each time. A reverse proxy must preserve the required connection behaviour and timeouts, which is why these services can need route-specific handling.
terms.wireguard: WireGuard creates the encrypted network link between the public VPS and the Raspberry Pi. Caddy reaches the Pi at 10.90.0.2 through this tunnel, avoiding a public application route to the residential address.
terms.wireguard-allowedips: WireGuard AllowedIPs defines which destination addresses are routed to a peer and which source addresses are accepted from it. Both peers in this setup use only the other tunnel endpoint's /32 address; this narrows routing but does not replace a port-level firewall.
terms.wireguard-keepalive: Persistent keepalive makes a WireGuard peer send a small packet periodically even when no application traffic is flowing. The Pi uses it to keep the home router's NAT mapping usable so the VPS can continue reaching the tunnel after idle periods.
